chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Al-Qasim, the companion of Al-Mufazzal, and he was a truthful man, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A group in the Masjid publicize us and publicize themselves; those are not from us, nor are we from them. I go away and hide, but they uncover my veil. May Allah violate their veils. They say: 'Is he an Imam?' By Allah, I am not an Imam except for the one who obeys me; as for the one who disobeys me, I am not an Imam for him. Why do they cling to my name? Should they not cease mentioning my name from their mouths? By Allah, may He not gather me and them in one abode.'

key_terms.أُولَئِكَ: those (demonstrative pronoun referring to the group)
key_terms.يَشْهَرُونَ: to publicize or make known openly

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for being considered under the Imamate of the Prophet's family according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) critiques the phenomenon of *shuhrah* (public fame) among those claiming affiliation with the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing between genuine spiritual authority and self-aggrandizement. He highlights the conditional nature of leadership, noting that obedience defines the relationship, while expressing a divine wish to separate from those who misuse his name for personal prestige. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on humility and the distinction between the Imam's intrinsic authority and the contingent loyalty of followers.
